items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: She had engaged Buddy Banks who had been with me before, on bass.

ctx.x: Everything went along smoothly until the end of June, and we had been playing every afternoon and night since the 15th that month. Then we found out that the boss didn't have a working permit for us.

Why, I cannot say, because he must have known that it was necessary. Then he tried to get the permits and we found out that he had been in trouble with the government about taxes and had put all of his business in the name of his girl friend whom he had been living with for years. The result was that we were refused working permits, and the 9th of July, we all left Belgium. Buddy Banks had married a Swiss girl, so he went to Switzerland, and I came to Paris.

Home was wherever I hung my hat, and I travelled with all my earthly belongings. When Lily and I got together, she had quite a few things also. We had left a few bags in Switzerland and when the gig in Blankenberge fell through, we decided that Lily should do to Switzerland to get the suit-cases we had left there and I would go to Paris with the things we had with us.
